handoffs.summary: Populated the four DevFlow memory files with verified DartHub state read from the repo at E:\coding\darthub (branch feature/darthub-design-implementation, 5 commits, dirty working tree). PROJECT.md records purpose, users/workflows, hard constraints and 11 explicit source contradictions (stale directory layout in .claude/architecture.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; engine at src/game-engine not src/game; three conflicting completion states; docs/API.md paths and Socket.IO event names not implemented; missing /login route; missing CareerQuestProgress Prisma model; shadcn/ui absent; test framework doc stale; realtime bound to NeutralScoreMode; matchmaking module unwired). CURRENT_STATE.md separates committed implementation from uncommitted work (the entire design-implementation plan output is uncommitted), lists ten known issues, and states explicitly that the test suite, build, lint, typecheck and Playwright were NOT run. ARCHITECTURE.md documents the real flat-feature-folder layout, the REST/WS/camera/board data flows with path:line references, and eight observed porous boundaries. DOCUMENTATION-INDEX.md indexes the real documentation set and lists ten missing-document observations. No file outside .devflow/ was created, modified or deleted; no git command other than status/log/diff/ls-tree was run; no commit, add or branch operation.

handoffs.summary: Review pass on the four DevFlow memory files performed in-session by the orchestrator session after the devflow-orchestrator review subagent was aborted by the user. Result: the deliverable stands - all four files are written and every load-bearing claim that was checked could be confirmed against the repository. The task is recorded as partial because the subagent's wider sampled-claim verification was cut short and was not reproduced in full. Cause of the high resource consumption: the repository surface was read twice. The project-memory-steward pass consumed 91 tool calls and roughly 103k tokens reading docs/ src/ tests/ plans and the git diffs; the review subagent then re-read the same files to re-derive the steward's already cited facts because it had no access to the steward's evidence trail and was instructed to open ten or more referenced files individually. Cost therefore scaled with agents times repo size instead of reusing the cited path:line evidence and spot-checking only the load-bearing claims - five targeted shell checks confirmed the same load-bearing claims at a fraction of the cost.

No disputed item changed a conclusion in the four files - every dispute was a wrong line anchor or an imprecise citation, so the deliverable stands. Review recorded as R-001 pass.

The code-reviewer assignment checked 58 citations (50 PASS, 8 DISPUTED); the orchestrator independently re-verified all 8 disputes against the repository and confirmed every one, then corrected them in the four files - a wrong line anchor in every case, never a wrong conclusion. 22 corrected anchors were re-verified against file content after editing. The two workers used were project-memory-steward (authored the deliverable) and code-reviewer (independent verification); no product code was written and no file outside .devflow/ was modified. handoffs.summary: Implemented the game-engine throw ledger, replay-based recalculation and the undo/correct operations. RecordedThrow {playerId, points, segment?, bust} is carried in MatchState alongside a corrections audit list; visit grouping is DERIVED (MatchVisit + getVisits()), never stored, so it cannot go stale. GameEngine extracts recordThrow's body into a private applyToDraft(draft, record) that owns the dart counters, the turn advance and the completion check, and replay calls applyToDraft - not the mode directly - because turn order, counters and status are engine-owned (review finding C1). startMatch now retains playerIds, a copy of the MatchConfig and the matchId, and replay re-seeds from those via createSeedDraft, never via startMatch, so the checkout rule and leg structure survive (C2). GameEngineBustError extends GameEngineStateError and is thrown only for the bust case, so replay can distinguish a bust from a real failure while every existing error assertion still passes (C3). A correction is refused - changing neither state nor ledger - when the index is missing, the match is completed, the replacement would bust the corrected dart, or it would make a later recorded dart bust that previously did not (C4). undoLastThrow works on a completed match, so the match-winning dart can be undone (C5). A correction that changes the match result is audited via an optional mode-owned resultSignature hook, keeping the mechanism mode-agnostic (C6). The ledger is cloned in both directions between state and draft so a mode cannot mutate it by reference, and the payload bound is documented (I4). StandardMode was changed - outside the stated file list - because C3 and C6 require it.

The orchestrator then ran an INDEPENDENT verification of 11 behaviours: ledger length differs from throwCount on a bust while the score and counters stay untouched; undo restores the exact prior state by full-state toEqual; undo of the match-winning dart returns status to inProgress with the turn restored; a correction never moves a dart between players; a refused correction leaves the whole state unchanged; the double-out rule SURVIVES a replay (proved by a 40-with-no-segment still busting at 40 left after an undo and a correct - if the config had been lost, the mode would have fallen back to straight out and won instead); cricket marks, the around-the-clock target index and shanghai rounds are each restored exactly by undo; the state stays JSON-safe; visits are derived and not stored. Three audit rules verified: a plain turn-in-progress correction is not audited, a correction that removes a leg win is audited, a correction in a finished turn is audited with dartIndex, playerId, previousPoints and newPoints.
